column1: “My dear, you flatter me. I certainly _have_ had my share of beauty, but I do not pretend to be anything extraordinary now. When a woman has five grown-up daughters, she ought to give over thinking of her own beauty.”
column2: “亲爱的，你过奖了。我当然有我的美丽，但我现在不假装什么了不起。当一个女人有五个成年女儿时，她应该放弃对自己美丽的思考。”

column1: “But consider your daughters. Only think what an establishment it would be for one of them. Sir William and Lady Lucas are determined to go, merely on that account; for in general, you know, they visit no new comers. Indeed you must go, for it will be impossible for _us_ to visit him, if you do not.”
column2: “但是想想你的女儿们吧。只要想一想，这对她们中的一个来说会是一个什么样的场所。威廉爵士和卢卡斯夫人决定去，只是因为这个原因；因为一般来说，你知道，他们不会拜访新来的人。事实上，你必须去，因为如果你不去，我们就不可能去拜访他。”

column1: “You are over scrupulous, surely. I dare say Mr. Bingley will be very glad to see you; and I will send a few lines by you to assure him of my hearty consent to his marrying whichever he chooses of the girls--though I must throw in a good word for my little Lizzy.”
column2: “你确实太谨慎了。我敢说彬格莱先生见到你一定会很高兴的；我会由你寄几行信来向他保证，我衷心同意他与他选择的任何一个女孩结婚——不过我必须为我的小莉齐说几句好话。”

column1: “I desire you will do no such thing. Lizzy is not a bit better than the others: and I am sure she is not half so handsome as Jane, nor half so good-humoured as Lydia. But you are always giving _her_ the preference.”
column2: “我希望你不要做这样的事。丽兹并不比其他人好一点：而且我确信她没有简一半英俊，也没有莉迪亚一半好脾气。但你总是偏爱她。”

column1: “Mr. Bennet, how can you abuse your own children in such a way? You take delight in vexing me. You have no compassion on my poor nerves.”
column2: “班纳特先生，你怎么能这样虐待你自己的孩子？你以惹恼我为乐。你对我可怜的神经毫无同情心。”

column1: “You mistake me, my dear. I have a high respect for your nerves. They are my old friends. I have heard you mention them with consideration these twenty years at least.”
column2: “你误会我了，亲爱的。我非常尊重你的神经质。他们是我的老朋友。至少这二十年来我听你提到他们时很体贴。”

column1: Mr. Bennet was so odd a mixture of quick parts, sarcastic humour, reserve, and caprice, that the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character. _Her_ mind was less difficult to develope. She was a woman of mean understanding, little information, and uncertain temper. When she was discontented, she fancied herself nervous. The business of her life was to get her daughters married: its solace was visiting and news.
column2: 班纳特先生性格古怪，集快感、讽刺性幽默、矜持和任性于一身，三年二十年的经历不足以让他的妻子了解他的性格。她的心智不那么难以发展。她是一个理解力薄弱、见识少、脾气不稳定的女人。当她不满的时候，她觉得自己很紧张。她一生的事业就是让女儿们结婚：来访和新闻是她的安慰。

column1: Mr. Bennet was among the earliest of those who waited on Mr. Bingley. He had always intended to visit him, though to the last always assuring his wife that he should not go; and till the evening after the visit was paid she had no knowledge of it. It was then disclosed in the following manner. Observing his second daughter employed in trimming a hat, he suddenly addressed her with,--
column2: 班纳特先生是最早侍候彬格莱先生的人之一。他一直打算去看望他，尽管到最后总是向他的妻子保证他不应该去。直到拜访后的那天晚上，她才知道这件事。然后以如下方式披露。看着二女儿正在剪帽子，他突然对她说道：

column1: “But you forget, mamma,” said Elizabeth, “that we shall meet him at the assemblies, and that Mrs. Long has promised to introduce him.”
column2: “但是你忘了，妈妈，”伊丽莎白说，“我们会在集会上见到他，而且朗夫人已经答应介绍他了。”

column1: “I do not believe Mrs. Long will do any such thing. She has two nieces of her own. She is a selfish, hypocritical woman, and I have no opinion of her.”
column2: “我不相信龙太太会做出这样的事。她自己有两个侄女，她是一个自私、虚伪的女人，我对她没有意见。”

column1: “Ay, so it is,” cried her mother, “and Mrs. Long does not come back till the day before; so, it will be impossible for her to introduce him, for she will not know him herself.”
column2: “哎呀，是这样的，”她母亲喊道，“朗太太直到前一天才回来；所以，她不可能介绍他，因为她自己也不认识他。”

column1: “I honour your circumspection. A fortnight’s acquaintance is certainly very little. One cannot know what a man really is by the end of a fortnight. But if _we_ do not venture, somebody else will; and after all, Mrs. Long and her nieces must stand their chance; and, therefore, as she will think it an act of kindness, if you decline the office, I will take it on myself.”
column2: “我尊重你的谨慎。两周的熟识肯定是很少的。两周结束后，一个人无法知道一个男人到底是什么样的。但如果我们不冒险，其他人会的。毕竟，朗夫人和她的侄女们必须抓住机会；因此，因为她会认为这是一种善意的行为，如果你拒绝担任这个职务，我会亲自承担。”

column1: “What can be the meaning of that emphatic exclamation?” cried he. “Do you consider the forms of introduction, and the stress that is laid on them, as nonsense? I cannot quite agree with you _there_. What say you, Mary? For you are a young lady of deep reflection, I know, and read great books, and make extracts.”
column2: “这声强调的感叹是什么意思？”他喊道。 “你是否认为介绍的形式以及对它们施加的压力是无稽之谈？我不太同意你的观点。玛丽，你怎么说？因为我知道，你是一位善于反思的年轻女士，读过好书，还摘录过。”

column1: “I am sorry to hear _that_; but why did you not tell me so before? If I had known as much this morning, I certainly would not have called on him. It is very unlucky; but as I have actually paid the visit, we cannot escape the acquaintance now.”
column2: “听到这个消息我很遗憾；但是你为什么之前不告诉我呢？如果我今天早上就知道这么多，我肯定不会去拜访他。这很不幸；但由于我确实拜访过，所以我们现在无法摆脱熟人。”

column1: The astonishment of the ladies was just what he wished--that of Mrs. Bennet perhaps surpassing the rest; though when the first tumult of joy was over, she began to declare that it was what she had expected all the while.
column2: 女士们的惊讶正是他所希望的——班纳特夫人的惊讶也许超过了其他人；尽管当第一次的欢乐结束后，她开始宣称这正是她一直所期待的。

column1: “How good it was in you, my dear Mr. Bennet! But I knew I should persuade you at last. I was sure you loved your girls too well to neglect such an acquaintance. Well, how pleased I am! And it is such a good joke, too, that you should have gone this morning, and never said a word about it till now.”
column2: “你真好，我亲爱的班纳特先生！但我知道我最终应该说服你。我相信你太爱你的女儿们了，不能忽视这样一个熟人。好吧，我多么高兴！这也是一个很好的笑话，你今天早上应该走了，直到现在才对这件事只字不提。”

column1: “Now, Kitty, you may cough as much as you choose,” said Mr. Bennet; and, as he spoke, he left the room, fatigued with the raptures of his wife.
column2: “现在，基蒂，你想咳嗽多少就咳嗽多少，”班纳特先生说。说完，他离开了房间，妻子的狂喜让他疲惫不堪。

column1: “What an excellent father you have, girls,” said she, when the door was shut. “I do not know how you will ever make him amends for his kindness; or me either, for that matter. At our time of life, it is not so pleasant, I can tell you, to be making new acquaintances every day; but for your sakes we would do anything. Lydia, my love, though you _are_ the youngest, I dare say Mr. Bingley will dance with you at the next ball.”
column2: “姑娘们，你们有一个多么优秀的父亲啊，”门关上后，她说道。 “我不知道你会如何补偿他的好意，也不知道我也一样。我可以告诉你，在我们这个年纪，每天结识新朋友并不是那么令人愉快；但为了你，我们愿意做任何事。莉迪亚，我的爱人，虽然你是最小的，我敢说彬格莱先生会在下一次舞会上和你一起跳舞。”

column1: The rest of the evening was spent in conjecturing how soon he would return Mr. Bennet’s visit, and determining when they should ask him to dinner.
column2: 晚上剩下的时间都花在猜测他多久会回来班纳特先生的拜访，并确定他们什么时候应该请他吃饭。

column1: Not all that Mrs. Bennet, however, with the assistance of her five daughters, could ask on the subject, was sufficient to draw from her husband any satisfactory description of Mr. Bingley. They attacked him in various ways, with barefaced questions, ingenious suppositions, and distant surmises; but he eluded the skill of them all; and they were at last obliged to accept the second-hand intelligence of their neighbour, Lady Lucas. Her report was highly favourable. Sir William had been delighted with him. He was quite young, wonderfully handsome, extremely agreeable, and, to crown the whole, he meant to be at the next assembly with a large party. Nothing could be more delightful! To be fond of dancing was a certain step towards falling in love; and very lively hopes of Mr. Bingley’s heart were entertained.
column2: 然而，班纳特夫人在五个女儿的帮助下，就这个问题所提出的问题，并不足以从她丈夫那里得到对彬格莱先生的任何令人满意的描述。他们以各种方式攻击他，有赤裸裸的问题，有巧妙的假设，还有遥远的猜测；但他却躲过了所有人的技巧。他们最终不得不接受邻居卢卡斯夫人的二手情报。她的报告非常有利。威廉爵士对他很满意。他很年轻，非常英俊，非常和蔼可亲，最重要的是，他打算参加下一次的大型聚会。没有什么比这更令人愉快的了！喜欢跳舞是迈向恋爱的必经之路；彬格莱先生内心的强烈希望得到了满足。

column1: “If I can but see one of my daughters happily settled at Netherfield,” said Mrs. Bennet to her husband, “and all the others equally well married, I shall have nothing to wish for.”
column2: “如果我只能看到我的一个女儿在尼日斐花园幸福地定居下来，”班纳特夫人对她的丈夫说，“并且所有其他女儿都同样嫁得很好，我就没有什么可希望的了。”

column1: In a few days Mr. Bingley returned Mr. Bennet’s visit, and sat about ten minutes with him in his library. He had entertained hopes of being admitted to a sight of the young ladies, of whose beauty he had heard much; but he saw only the father. The ladies were somewhat more fortunate, for they had the advantage of ascertaining, from an upper window, that he wore a blue coat and rode a black horse.
column2: 几天后，宾利先生回访了班纳特先生，并在图书馆里与他一起坐了大约十分钟。他曾希望能见到那些年轻女士，他曾多次听说过她们的美丽。但他只看到了父亲。女士们稍微幸运一些，因为她们可以从楼上的窗户看出他穿着蓝色外套，骑着一匹黑马。

column1: An invitation to dinner was soon afterwards despatched; and already had Mrs. Bennet planned the courses that were to do credit to her housekeeping, when an answer arrived which deferred it all. Mr. Bingley was obliged to be in town the following day, and consequently unable to accept the honour of their invitation, etc. Mrs. Bennet was quite disconcerted. She could not imagine what business he could have in town so soon after his arrival in Hertfordshire; and she began to fear that he might always be flying about from one place to another, and never settled at Netherfield as he ought to be. Lady Lucas quieted her fears a little by starting the idea of his
column2: 不久之后就发出了一份晚餐邀请函。班纳特夫人已经计划好了要为她的家政做贡献的课程，当一个答复到来时，这一切都推迟了。彬格莱先生第二天必须到城里，因此无法接受他们的邀请，等等。班纳特夫人感到非常不安。她无法想象他刚抵达赫特福德郡这么快就到城里来做什么；她开始担心他可能总是从一个地方飞到另一个地方，而从未像他应该的那样在尼日斐花园定居。卢卡斯夫人开始了他的想法，稍稍平息了她的恐惧。

column1: being gone to London only to get a large party for the ball; and a report soon followed that Mr. Bingley was to bring twelve ladies and seven gentlemen with him to the assembly. The girls grieved over such a number of ladies; but were comforted the day before the ball by hearing that, instead of twelve, he had brought only six with him from London, his five sisters and a cousin. And when the party entered the assembly-room, it consisted of only five altogether: Mr. Bingley, his two sisters, the husband of the eldest, and another young man.
column2: 去伦敦只是为了举办一场大型舞会；很快就有报道称宾利先生将带着十二位女士和七位先生参加集会。女孩们为这么多的女士感到悲伤。但在舞会前一天，当得知他从伦敦只带来了六个人而不是十二个，即他的五个姐妹和一个表弟时，我们感到很欣慰。当一行人进入会议室时，总共只有五个人：彬格莱先生、他的两个姐妹、长子的丈夫和另一个年轻人。

column1: Mr. Bingley was good-looking and gentlemanlike: he had a pleasant countenance, and easy, unaffected manners. His sisters were fine women, with an air of decided fashion. His brother-in-law, Mr. Hurst, merely looked the gentleman; but his friend Mr. Darcy soon drew the attention of the room by his fine, tall person, handsome features, noble mien, and the report, which was in general circulation within five minutes after his entrance, of his having ten thousand a year. The gentlemen pronounced him to be a fine figure of a man, the ladies declared he was much handsomer than Mr. Bingley, and he was looked at with great admiration for about half the evening, till his manners gave a disgust which turned the tide of his popularity; for he was discovered to be proud, to be above his company, and above being pleased; and not all his large estate in Derbyshire could save him from having a most forbidding, disagreeable countenance, and being unworthy to be compared with his friend.
column2: 彬格莱先生相貌英俊，很有绅士风度：他有一张令人愉快的面容，举止从容、不做作。他的姐妹们都是漂亮的女人，有着坚定的时尚气息。他的姐夫赫斯特先生看上去只是个绅士。但他的朋友达西先生很快就引起了全场的注意，他身材高大，英俊的容貌，高贵的风度，以及他进来后五分钟内就广为流传的关于他年收入一万的报道。先生们称赞他是一个优秀的男人，女士们宣称他比彬格莱先生英俊得多，大约半个晚上人们都以极大的钦佩目光看着他，直到他的举止令人厌恶，这扭转了他受欢迎的趋势；因为人们发现他很骄傲，高高在上，不高兴。他在德比郡的大笔财产并不能挽救他的面容，他的面容极其令人生畏、令人不快，与他的朋友相比根本不值一提。

column1: Mr. Bingley had soon made himself acquainted with all the principal people in the room: he was lively and unreserved, danced every dance, was angry that the ball closed so early, and talked of giving one himself at Netherfield. Such amiable qualities must speak for themselves. What a contrast between him and his friend! Mr. Darcy danced only once with Mrs. Hurst and once with Miss Bingley, declined being introduced to any other lady, and spent the rest of the evening in walking about the room, speaking occasionally to one of his own party. His character was decided. He was the proudest, most disagreeable man in the world, and everybody hoped that he would never come there again. Amongst the most violent against him was Mrs. Bennet, whose dislike of his general behaviour was sharpened into particular resentment by his having slighted one of her daughters.
column2: 宾利先生很快就熟悉了房间里的所有主要人物：他活泼、毫无保留，每支舞都跳，对舞会这么早结束感到生气，并谈到自己要在尼日斐花园给自己一个机会。这种和蔼可亲的品质是不言而喻的。他和他的朋友之间形成了多么鲜明的对比啊！达西先生只和赫斯特夫人跳了一次舞，又和彬格莱小姐跳了一次舞，他拒绝被介绍给任何其他女士，晚上剩下的时间都在房间里走来走去，偶尔和他自己的一个人说话。他的性格已经决定了。他是世界上最骄傲、最令人讨厌的人，每个人都希望他永远不会再回到那里。对他最暴力的人之一是班纳特夫人，她对他一般行为的厌恶因他轻视了她的一个女儿而变得特别怨恨。

column1: Elizabeth Bennet had been obliged, by the scarcity of gentlemen, to sit down for two dances; and during part of that time, Mr. Darcy had been standing near enough for her to overhear a conversation between him and Mr. Bingley, who came from the dance for a few minutes to press his friend to join it.
column2: 由于缺少绅士，伊丽莎白·班纳特不得不坐下来参加两场舞会。在那段时间里，达西先生站得离她很近，足以让她无意中听到他和彬格莱先生之间的对话，彬格莱先生从舞会结束了几分钟，敦促他的朋友加入。

column1: “Come, Darcy,” said he, “I must have you dance. I hate to see you standing about by yourself in this stupid manner. You had much better dance.”
column2: “来吧，达西，”他说，“我一定要让你跳舞。我讨厌看到你一个人以这种愚蠢的方式站着。你最好跳舞。”

column1: “I certainly shall not. You know how I detest it, unless I am particularly acquainted with my partner. At such an assembly as this, it would be insupportable. Your sisters are engaged, and there is not another woman in the room whom it would not be a punishment to me to stand up with.”
column2: “我当然不会。你知道我有多讨厌它，除非我和我的伴侣特别熟悉。在这样的集会上，这是无法忍受的。你的姐妹们都订婚了，房间里没有另一个女人，如果我站起来，对我来说不是一种惩罚。”

column1: “I would not be so fastidious as you are,” cried Bingley, “for a kingdom! Upon my honour, I never met with so many pleasant girls in my life as I have this evening; and there are several of them, you see, uncommonly pretty.”
column2: “为了一个王国，”彬格莱喊道，“我不会像你那么挑剔！以我的名誉来说，我一生中从来没有像今晚这样遇到过这么多可爱的女孩；你看，其中有几个非常漂亮。”

column1: “Oh, she is the most beautiful creature I ever beheld! But there is one of her sisters sitting down just behind you, who is very pretty, and I dare say very agreeable. Do let me ask my partner to introduce you.”
column2: “哦，她是我见过的最美丽的生物！不过她的一个姐妹就坐在你后面，非常漂亮，我敢说非常讨人喜欢。请让我的搭档给你介绍一下。”

column1: “Which do you mean?” and turning round, he looked for a moment at Elizabeth, till, catching her eye, he withdrew his own, and coldly said, “She is tolerable: but not handsome enough to tempt _me_; and I am in no humour at present to give consequence to young ladies who are slighted by other men. You had better return to your partner and enjoy her smiles, for you are wasting your time with me.”
column2: “你什么意思？”他转过身，看了伊丽莎白一会儿，直到与她的目光相遇后，他收回了自己的目光，冷冷地说：“她还算可以，但还不够漂亮，不足以诱惑我。我现在没有心情去计较那些被其他男人轻视的年轻女士。你最好回到你的伴侣身边，享受她的微笑，因为你和我在一起是在浪费时间。”

column1: Mr. Bingley followed his advice. Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings towards him. She told the story, however, with great spirit among her friends; for she had a lively, playful disposition, which delighted in anything ridiculous.
column2: 宾利先生听从了他的建议。达西先生走开了。伊丽莎白对他仍然没有很亲切的感情。然而，她在朋友们面前兴高采烈地讲述了这个故事。因为她性情活泼、顽皮，对任何荒唐的事都感到高兴。

column1: The evening altogether passed off pleasantly to the whole family. Mrs. Bennet had seen her eldest daughter much admired by the Netherfield party. Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice, and she had been distinguished by his sisters. Jane was as much gratified by this as her mother could be, though in a quieter way. Elizabeth felt Jane’s pleasure. Mary had heard herself mentioned to Miss Bingley as the most accomplished girl in the neighbourhood; and Catherine and Lydia had been fortunate enough to be never without partners, which was all that they had yet learnt to care for at a ball. They returned, therefore, in good spirits to Longbourn, the village where they lived, and of which they were the principal inhabitants. They found Mr. Bennet still up. With a book, he was regardless of time; and on the present occasion he had a good deal of curiosity as to the event of an evening which had raised such splendid expectations. He had rather hoped that all his wife’s views on the stranger would be disappointed; but he soon found that he had a very different story to hear.
column2: 整个晚上，全家人都过得很愉快。班纳特夫人看到她的大女儿深受尼日斐花园党的钦佩。彬格莱先生曾与她共舞过两次，她在他的姐妹们中脱颖而出。简和她母亲一样对此感到非常满意，尽管是以一种比较安静的方式。伊丽莎白感受到了简的高兴。玛丽曾听宾利小姐提到自己是附近最有成就的女孩。凯瑟琳和莉迪亚很幸运，从来没有没有舞伴，这就是她们在舞会上学会关心的一切。因此，他们兴高采烈地回到了朗伯恩，他们居住的村庄，也是他们的主要居民。他们发现班纳特先生还没睡。有了书，他不顾时间；有了书，他不顾时间；此时此刻，他对这个引起如此美好期望的夜晚感到非常好奇。他宁愿希望他的妻子对这个陌生人的所有看法都会失望。但他很快发现他听到的是一个截然不同的故事。

column1: “Oh, my dear Mr. Bennet,” as she entered the room, “we have had a most delightful evening, a most excellent ball. I wish you had been there. Jane was so admired, nothing could be like it. Everybody said how well she looked; and Mr. Bingley thought her quite beautiful, and danced with her twice. Only think of _that_, my dear: he actually danced with her twice; and she was the only creature in the room that he asked a second time. First of all, he asked Miss Lucas. I was so vexed to see him stand up with her; but, however, he did not admire her at all; indeed, nobody can, you know; and he seemed quite struck with Jane as she was going down the dance. So he inquired who she was, and got introduced, and asked her for the two next. Then, the two third he danced with Miss King, and the two fourth with Maria Lucas, and the two fifth with Jane again, and the two sixth with Lizzy, and the _Boulanger_----”
column2: “哦，我亲爱的班纳特先生，”当她走进房间时，“我们度过了一个最愉快的夜晚，一个最精彩的舞会。我希望你也在场。简是如此受人钦佩，没有什么比这更好的了。每个人都说她看起来多么漂亮；彬格莱先生认为她很漂亮，并与她共舞了两次。只要想一想，亲爱的：他实际上与她共舞了两次；她是房间里唯一一个他第二次邀请的生物。首先，他问卢卡斯小姐，我很恼火地看到他和她站在一起；但是，事实上，没有人能欣赏她；当她参加舞会时，他似乎对她很感兴趣，于是他向她介绍了接下来的两个，然后是与玛丽亚·卢卡斯一起跳舞的第二个，第五个是与简跳舞的，还有第六个。 _布朗格_----”

column1: “If he had had any compassion for _me_,” cried her husband impatiently, “he would not have danced half so much! For God’s sake, say no more of his partners. O that he had sprained his ancle in the first dance!”
column2: “如果他对我有一点同情心，”她丈夫不耐烦地喊道，“他就不会跳这么多了！看在上帝的分上，不要再说他的舞伴了。哦，但愿他在第一支舞中扭伤了自己的脚踝！”

column1: “Oh, my dear,” continued Mrs. Bennet, “I am quite delighted with him. He is so excessively handsome! and his sisters are charming women. I never in my life saw anything more elegant than their dresses. I dare say the lace upon Mrs. Hurst’s gown----”
column2: “哦，亲爱的，”班纳特太太继续说，“我对他很满意。他太英俊了！他的姐妹们都是迷人的女人。我一生中从未见过比她们的衣服更优雅的衣服。我敢说赫斯特太太礼服上的花边——”

column1: Here she was interrupted again. Mr. Bennet protested against any description of finery. She was therefore obliged to seek another branch of the subject, and related, with much bitterness of spirit, and some exaggeration, the shocking rudeness of Mr. Darcy.
column2: 说到这里，她又被打断了。班纳特先生抗议任何对华丽服饰的描述。因此，她不得不寻找这个话题的另一个分支，并以极大的痛苦和一些夸张的态度讲述了达西先生令人震惊的粗鲁行为。

column1: “But I can assure you,” she added, “that Lizzy does not lose much by not suiting _his_ fancy; for he is a most disagreeable, horrid man, not at all worth pleasing. So high and so conceited, that there was no enduring him! He walked here, and he walked there, fancying himself so very great! Not handsome enough to dance with! I wish you had been there, my dear, to have given him one of your set-downs. I quite detest the man.”
column2: “但是我可以向你保证，”她补充道，“丽兹不会因不符合他的幻想而损失太多；因为他是一个最令人讨厌、最可怕的人，根本不值得取悦。他如此高傲，如此自负，以至于没有人能忍受他！他走来走去，幻想自己如此伟大！不够英俊，无法与之共舞！我希望你当时在场，亲爱的，给他一个你的下场。我非常讨厌那个男人。”

column1: When Jane and Elizabeth were alone, the former, who had been cautious in her praise of Mr. Bingley before, expressed to her sister how very much she admired him.
column2: 当简和伊丽莎白单独在一起时，以前对彬格莱先生的赞扬很谨慎的简，向她的妹妹表达了她对他的钦佩之情。

column1: “He is just what a young man ought to be,” said she, “sensible, good-humoured, lively; and I never saw such happy manners! so much ease, with such perfect good breeding!”
column2: “他正是年轻人该有的样子，”她说，“懂事、幽默、活泼；我从来没有见过如此快乐的举止！如此轻松，有如此完美的良好教养！”

column1: “He is also handsome,” replied Elizabeth, “which a young man ought likewise to be if he possibly can. His character is thereby complete.”
column2: “他也很英俊，”伊丽莎白回答道，“如果可能的话，一个年轻人也应该如此。因此，他的性格是完整的。”

column1: “Did not you? _I_ did for you. But that is one great difference between us. Compliments always take _you_ by surprise, and _me_ never. What could be more natural than his asking you again? He could not help seeing that you were about five times as pretty as every other woman in the room. No thanks to his gallantry for that. Well, he certainly is very agreeable, and I give you leave to like him. You have liked many a stupider person.”
column2: “不是吗？我是为你做的。但这就是我们之间的一个巨大区别。恭维总是让你感到惊讶，而我却从来没有。还有什么比他再次询问你更自然的呢？他情不自禁地发现你比房间里其他女人漂亮五倍。这并不感谢他的殷勤。好吧，他确实很和蔼可亲，我允许你喜欢他。你喜欢过很多愚蠢的人。”

column1: “Oh, you are a great deal too apt, you know, to like people in general. You never see a fault in anybody. All the world are good and agreeable in your eyes. I never heard you speak ill of a human being in my life.”
column2: “哦，你知道，你太容易喜欢一般人了。你从不看任何人的缺点。在你眼里，整个世界都是美好的、令人愉快的。我一生中从未听你说过任何人的坏话。”

column1: “I know you do: and it is _that_ which makes the wonder. With _your_ good sense, to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others! Affectation of candour is common enough; one meets with it everywhere. But to be candid without ostentation or design,--to take the good of everybody’s character and make it still better, and say nothing of the bad,--belongs to you alone. And so, you like this man’s sisters, too, do you? Their manners are not equal to his.”
column2: “我知道你是这么做的：正是这一点才令人惊奇。以你的理智，对别人的愚蠢和胡言乱语如此诚实地视而不见！坦率的表现是很常见的；到处都可以遇到。但坦率而不炫耀或设计，——汲取每个人性格的优点，使其变得更好，不说不好的——只属于你一个人。所以，你喜欢这个人的姐妹们，你们也一样吗？她们的举止不如他。”

column1: “Certainly not, at first; but they are very pleasing women when you converse with them. Miss Bingley is to live with her brother, and keep his house; and I am much mistaken if we shall not find a very charming neighbour in her.”
column2: “当然不是，一开始；但是当你与她们交谈时，她们是非常讨人喜欢的女人。彬格莱小姐要和她哥哥住在一起，并看管他的房子；如果我们在她身上找不到一个非常迷人的邻居，那我就大错特错了。”

column1: Elizabeth listened in silence, but was not convinced: their behaviour at the assembly had not been calculated to please in general; and with more quickness of observation and less pliancy of temper than her sister, and with a judgment, too, unassailed by any attention to herself, she was very little disposed to approve them. They were, in fact, very fine ladies; not deficient in good-humour when they were pleased, nor in the power of being agreeable where they chose it; but proud and conceited. They were rather handsome; had been educated in one of the first private seminaries in town; had a fortune of twenty thousand pounds; were in the habit of spending more than they ought, and of associating with people of rank; and were, therefore, in every respect entitled to think well of themselves and meanly of others. They were of a respectable family in the north of England; a circumstance more deeply impressed on their memories than that their brother’s fortune and their own had been acquired by trade.
column2: 伊丽莎白默默地听着，但并不相信：他们在集会上的行为并不是为了取悦所有人。她的观察力比她姐姐更敏锐，但脾气却比她姐姐更不温顺，而且她的判断力也不受任何对自己的关注的影响，所以她不太愿意赞同他们。事实上，她们都是非常优秀的女士。当他们高兴的时候，并不缺乏幽默感；当他们选择的时候，也不缺乏随和的能力；但骄傲自负。他们相当英俊；曾在城里最早的私立神学院之一接受教育；拥有两万英镑的财产；习惯于过度消费，并与有地位的人交往；因此，我们在各方面都有权看好自己而看低他人。他们出身于英格兰北部一个受人尊敬的家庭。与他们兄弟的财产和他们自己的财产是通过贸易获得的相比，这种情况给他们留下了更深刻的印象。

column1: Mr. Bingley inherited property to the amount of nearly a hundred thousand pounds from his father, who had intended to purchase an estate, but did not live to do it. Mr. Bingley intended it likewise, and sometimes made choice of his county; but, as he was now provided with a good house and the liberty of a manor, it was doubtful to many of those who best knew the easiness of his temper, whether he might not spend the remainder of his days at Netherfield, and leave the next generation to purchase.
column2: 宾利先生从他父亲那里继承了近十万英镑的财产，他父亲原本打算购买一处庄园，但未能活着。彬格莱先生也有同样的意图，有时他会选择他的县。但是，由于他现在拥有一栋好房子和庄园的自由，许多最了解他脾气暴躁的人都怀疑他是否会在尼日斐花园度过余生，并留给下一代购买。

column1: His sisters were very anxious for his having an estate of his own; but though he was now established only as a tenant, Miss Bingley was by no means unwilling to preside at his table; nor was Mrs. Hurst, who had married a man of more fashion than fortune, less disposed to consider his house as her home when it suited her. Mr. Bingley had not been of age two years when he was tempted, by an accidental recommendation, to look at Netherfield House. He did look at it, and into it, for half an hour; was pleased with the situation and the principal rooms, satisfied with what the owner said in its praise, and took it immediately.
column2: 他的姐妹们非常渴望他拥有自己的庄园。尽管他现在只是作为一个佃户，彬格莱小姐却一点也不愿意主持他的餐桌。赫斯特夫人嫁给了一个比财富更时尚的男人，当她觉得合适的时候，她也毫不犹豫地把他的房子当作她的家。宾利先生在一次偶然的推荐下，想去参观尼日斐宫时，还不满两岁。他确实看了半个小时。对情况和正房很满意，对业主夸奖的话很满意，立即入住。

column1: Between him and Darcy there was a very steady friendship, in spite of a great opposition of character. Bingley was endeared to Darcy by the easiness, openness, and ductility of his temper, though no disposition could offer a greater contrast to his own, and though with his own he never appeared dissatisfied. On the strength of Darcy’s regard, Bingley had the firmest reliance, and of his judgment the highest opinion. In understanding, Darcy was the superior. Bingley was by no means deficient; but Darcy was clever. He was at the same time haughty, reserved, and fastidious; and his manners, though well bred, were not inviting. In that respect his friend had greatly the advantage. Bingley was sure of being liked wherever he appeared; Darcy was continually giving offence.
column2: 尽管性格截然相反，他和达西之间却有着非常稳定的友谊。彬格莱的性格随和、开放、灵活，深受达西的喜爱，尽管没有什么性格能与他的性格形成更大的反差，尽管他对自己的性格从来没有表现出不满。宾利对达西的尊重是最坚定的，对他的判断也是最高的评价。在理解上，达西更胜一筹。宾利绝不是有缺陷的人。但达西很聪明。他同时又傲慢、矜持、挑剔。他的举止虽然很有教养，但并不讨人喜欢。在这方面，他的朋友有很大的优势。宾利无论出现在哪里，都肯定会受到人们的喜爱。达西不断地冒犯别人。

column1: The manner in which they spoke of the Meryton assembly was sufficiently characteristic. Bingley had never met with pleasanter people or prettier girls in his life; everybody had been most kind and attentive to him; there had been no formality, no stiffness; he had soon felt acquainted with all the room; and as to Miss Bennet, he could not conceive an angel more beautiful. Darcy, on the contrary, had seen a collection of people in whom there was little beauty and no fashion, for none of whom he had felt the smallest interest, and from none received either attention or pleasure. Miss Bennet he acknowledged to be pretty; but she smiled too much.
column2: 他们谈论梅里顿集会的方式很有特色。宾利一生中从未遇到过比他更令人愉快的人或比他更漂亮的女孩。每个人都对他非常友善和殷勤。没有拘谨，没有僵硬；很快他就熟悉了整个房间。至于班纳特小姐，他想不出比她更美丽的天使了。相反，达西看到了一群人，他们没有什么美感，也没有什么时尚，他对他们中没有一个人感到有丝毫兴趣，也没有人从他们那里得到任何关注或快乐。他承认班纳特小姐很漂亮。但她笑得太过分了。

column1: Mrs. Hurst and her sister allowed it to be so; but still they admired her and liked her, and pronounced her to be a sweet girl, and one whom they should not object to know more of. Miss Bennet was therefore established as a sweet girl; and their brother felt authorized by such commendation to think of her as he chose.
column2: 赫斯特夫人和她的妹妹允许这样的事情发生。但他们仍然钦佩她、喜欢她，并称她是一位可爱的女孩，他们不应该反对更多地了解她。因此，班纳特小姐被认为是一个可爱的女孩。他们的兄弟觉得受到了这样的赞扬，就可以按照自己的选择来看待她。

column1: Within a short walk of Longbourn lived a family with whom the Bennets were particularly intimate. Sir William Lucas had been formerly in trade in Meryton, where he had made a tolerable fortune, and risen to the honour of knighthood by an address to the king during his mayoralty. The distinction had, perhaps, been felt too strongly. It had given him a disgust to his business and to his residence in a small market town; and, quitting them both, he had removed with his family to a house about a mile from Meryton, denominated from that period Lucas Lodge; where he could think with pleasure of his own importance, and, unshackled by business, occupy himself solely in being civil to all the world. For, though elated by his rank, it did not render him supercilious; on the contrary, he was all attention to everybody. By nature inoffensive, friendly, and obliging, his presentation at St. James’s had made him courteous.
column2: 距离朗伯恩不远的地方住着一户人家，班纳特一家与他们关系特别亲密。威廉·卢卡斯爵士以前曾在梅里顿做生意，在那里赚了一笔还算可观的财富，并在担任市长期间向国王发表讲话，获得了爵士的荣誉。也许人们对这种区别的感觉太强烈了。这让他对他的生意和他在一个小集镇的住所感到厌恶。他离开了他们两人，和家人一起搬到了距离梅里顿一英里的一所房子里，这座房子是从那个时期命名为卢卡斯洛奇的。在那里，他可以愉快地思考自己的重要性，并且不受生意的束缚，只专注于对全世界保持礼貌。因为，尽管他对自己的地位感到高兴，但这并没有使他傲慢。相反，他对每个人都很关注。他生性温和、友好、乐于助人，在圣詹姆斯教堂的演讲使他变得彬彬有礼。

column1: Lady Lucas was a very good kind of woman, not too clever to be a valuable neighbour to Mrs. Bennet. They had several children. The eldest of them, a sensible, intelligent young woman, about twenty-seven, was Elizabeth’s intimate friend.
column2: 卢卡斯夫人是一位非常善良的女人，虽然不太聪明，无法成为班纳特夫人的有价值的邻居。他们有几个孩子。其中最大的一个，是一位明智、聪明的年轻女子，大约二十七岁，是伊丽莎白的密友。

column1: “_You_ began the evening well, Charlotte,” said Mrs. Bennet, with civil self-command, to Miss Lucas. “_You_ were Mr. Bingley’s first choice.”
column2: “你这个晚上开得很好，夏洛特，”班纳特夫人以文明的自我控制方式对卢卡斯小姐说道。 “_你_是彬格莱先生的第一选择。”

column1: “Oh, you mean Jane, I suppose, because he danced with her twice. To be sure that _did_ seem as if he admired her--indeed, I rather believe he _did_--I heard something about it--but I hardly know what--something about Mr. Robinson.”
column2: “哦，我想你是说简，因为他和她跳了两次舞。可以肯定的是，他看起来确实很欣赏她——事实上，我宁愿相信他确实如此——我听说过一些关于这件事的事——但我几乎不知道是什么——关于罗宾逊先生的事。”

column1: “Perhaps you mean what I overheard between him and Mr. Robinson: did not I mention it to you? Mr. Robinson’s asking him how he liked our Meryton assemblies, and whether he did not think there were a great many pretty women in the room, and _which_ he thought the prettiest? and his answering immediately to the last question, ‘Oh, the eldest Miss Bennet, beyond a doubt: there cannot be two opinions on that point.’”
column2: “也许你的意思是我在他和罗宾逊先生之间无意中听到的：我没有向你提起过吗？罗宾逊先生问他是否喜欢我们梅里顿的集会，他是否认为房间里有很多漂亮的女人，他认为哪一个最漂亮？他立即回答了最后一个问题，“哦，大班纳特小姐，毫无疑问：在这一点上不能有两种意见。”

column1: “Upon my word! Well, that was very decided, indeed--that does seem as if--but, however, it may all come to nothing, you know.”
column2: “说实话！嗯，这确实是非常决定的——看起来确实像是——但是，然而，这一切都可能一事无成，你知道。”

column1: “_My_ overhearings were more to the purpose than _yours_, Eliza,” said Charlotte. “Mr. Darcy is not so well worth listening to as his friend, is he? Poor Eliza! to be only just _tolerable_.”
column2: “我的无意听证会比你的更能达到目的，伊丽莎，”夏洛特说。 “达西先生不像他的朋友那么值得听，不是吗？可怜的伊丽莎！只是_可以忍受_。”

column1: “I beg you will not put it into Lizzy’s head to be vexed by his ill-treatment, for he is such a disagreeable man that it would be quite a misfortune to be liked by him. Mrs. Long told me last night that he sat close to her for half an hour without once opening his lips.”
column2: “我请求你不要让莉兹因为他的虐待而烦恼，因为他是一个如此令人讨厌的人，被他喜欢将是一件很不幸的事。朗太太昨晚告诉我，他坐在她旁边有半个小时没有张开嘴唇。”

column1: “Miss Bingley told me,” said Jane, “that he never speaks much unless among his intimate acquaintance. With _them_ he is remarkably agreeable.”
column2: “彬格莱小姐告诉我，”简说，“除非是在熟人之间，否则他从不说话。与他们相处时，他非常和蔼可亲。”

column1: “I do not believe a word of it, my dear. If he had been so very agreeable, he would have talked to Mrs. Long. But I can guess how it was; everybody says that he is eat up with pride, and I dare say he had heard somehow that Mrs. Long does not keep a carriage, and had to come to the ball in a hack chaise.”
column2: “我一个字都不相信，亲爱的。如果他这么好意的话，他就会和朗夫人谈一谈了。但我能猜到是怎么回事；每个人都说他骄傲得要命，而且我敢说他不知何故听说朗夫人没有马车，不得不坐着一辆轻便马车来参加舞会。”

column1: “His pride,” said Miss Lucas, “does not offend _me_ so much as pride often does, because there is an excuse for it. One cannot wonder that so very fine a young man, with family, fortune, everything in his favour, should think highly of himself. If I may so express it, he has a _right_ to be proud.”
column2: “他的骄傲，”卢卡斯小姐说，“并不像骄傲经常那样冒犯我，因为这是有借口的。一个如此出色的年轻人，家庭、财富和一切都对他有利，他会高度评价自己，这是毫不奇怪的。如果我可以这样表达的话，他有权利感到骄傲。”

column1: “Pride,” observed Mary, who piqued herself upon the solidity of her reflections, “is a very common failing, I believe. By all that I have ever read, I am convinced that it is very common indeed; that human nature is particularly prone to it, and that there are very few of us who do not cherish a feeling of self-complacency on the score of some quality or other, real or imaginary. Vanity and pride are different things, though the words are often used synonymously. A person may be proud without being vain. Pride relates more to our opinion of ourselves; vanity to what we would have others think of us.”
column2: “骄傲，”玛丽说，她对自己的思考的可靠性感到兴奋，“我相信，这是一种非常普遍的缺点。根据我所读到的所有内容，我确信它确实非常普遍；人性特别容易产生这种感觉，而且我们中很少有人不怀着因某种品质或其他品质而感到自满的感觉，无论是真实的还是想象的。虚荣和骄傲是不同的东西，尽管这两个词经常被用作同义词。一个人可能会感到骄傲骄傲更多地与我们对自己的看法有关；虚荣心与我们希望别人对我们的看法有关。

column1: “If I were as rich as Mr. Darcy,” cried a young Lucas, who came with his sisters, “I should not care how proud I was. I would keep a pack of foxhounds, and drink a bottle of wine every day.”
column2: “如果我像达西先生一样富有，”和他的姐妹们一起来的年轻卢卡斯喊道，“我就不会在意自己有多骄傲。我会养一群猎狐犬，每天喝一瓶酒。”

column1: “Then you would drink a great deal more than you ought,” said Mrs. Bennet; “and if I were to see you at it, I should take away your bottle directly.”
column2: “那么你就会喝得比你应该喝的多得多，”班纳特太太说。 “如果我看到你，我会直接拿走你的瓶子。”

column1: The ladies of Longbourn soon waited on those of Netherfield. The visit was returned in due form. Miss Bennet’s pleasing manners grew on the good-will of Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley; and though the mother was found to be intolerable, and the younger sisters not worth speaking to, a wish of being better acquainted with _them_ was expressed towards the two eldest. By Jane this attention was received with the greatest pleasure; but Elizabeth still saw superciliousness in their treatment of everybody, hardly excepting even her sister, and could not like them; though their kindness to Jane, such as it was, had a value, as arising, in all probability, from the influence of their brother’s admiration. It was generally evident, whenever they met, that he _did_ admire her; and to _her_ it was equally evident that Jane was yielding to the preference which she had begun to entertain for him from the first, and was in a way to be very much in love; but she considered with pleasure that it was not likely to be discovered by the world in general, since Jane united with great strength of feeling, a composure of temper and an uniform cheerfulness of manner, which would guard her from the suspicions of the impertinent. She mentioned this to her friend, Miss Lucas.
column2: 朗伯恩的女士们很快就开始侍候尼日斐花园的女士们了。这次访问得到了适当的回报。班纳特小姐令人愉快的举止因赫斯特夫人和彬格莱小姐的善意而增长。尽管人们发现母亲难以忍受，妹妹们也不值得交谈，但还是向两个大女儿表达了与她们更加熟悉的愿望。简非常高兴地接受了这种关注。但伊丽莎白仍然看到他们对待每个人的态度都是傲慢的，甚至连她的妹妹也不例外，因此她不喜欢他们。尽管他们对简的善意是有价值的，因为很可能是受到他们兄弟的钦佩的影响。很明显，每当他们见面时，他确实很钦佩她。对她来说，同样明显的是，简正在屈服于她从一开始就开始对他产生的偏爱，并且在某种程度上非常爱他。但她高兴地认为，这不太可能被整个世界发现，因为简有着强烈的情感、冷静的脾气和一致的愉快的态度，这将使她免受无礼之人的怀疑。她向她的朋友卢卡斯小姐提到了这一点。

column1: “It may, perhaps, be pleasant,” replied Charlotte, “to be able to impose on the public in such a case; but it is sometimes a disadvantage to be so very guarded. If a woman conceals her affection with the same skill from the object of it, she may lose the opportunity of fixing him; and it will then be but poor consolation to believe the world equally in the dark. There is so much of gratitude or vanity in almost every attachment, that it is not safe to leave any to itself. We can all _begin_ freely--a slight preference is natural enough; but there are very few of us who have heart enough to be really in love without encouragement. In nine cases out of ten, a woman had better show _more_ affection than she feels. Bingley likes your sister undoubtedly; but he may never do more than like her, if she does not help him on.”
column2: “在这种情况下，能够向公众强加于人，或许是一件令人愉快的事，”夏洛特回答道，“但有时候，如此谨慎是一种缺点。如果一个女人以同样的技巧向对象隐藏自己的感情，她可能会失去修复他的机会；那么，在黑暗中同样相信这个世界将是微不足道的安慰。几乎每一种依恋中都存在着如此多的感激或虚荣，以至于把任何东西留给自己都是不安全的。我们都可以自由地开始——轻微的偏爱是很自然的；但是，在十有八九的情况下，很少有人有足够的心去爱你的妹妹，毫无疑问，宾利最好表现出比她自己感觉更多的感情；但如果她不帮助他，他可能永远不会比她更喜欢她。

Jane should therefore make the most of every half hour in which she can command his attention. When she is secure of him, there will be leisure for falling in love as much as she chooses.”

column1: “Your plan is a good one,” replied Elizabeth, “where nothing is in question but the desire of being well married; and if I were determined to get a rich husband, or any husband, I dare say I should adopt it. But these are not Jane’s feelings; she is not acting by design. As yet she cannot even be certain of the degree of her own regard, nor of its reasonableness. She has known him only a fortnight. She danced four dances with him at Meryton; she saw him one morning at his own house, and has since dined in company with him four times. This is not quite enough to make her understand his character.”
column2: “你的计划很好，”伊丽莎白答道，“除了渴望婚姻美满之外，没有什么问题；如果我决心找一个有钱的丈夫，或者任何一个丈夫，我敢说我应该采纳它。但这不是简的感觉；她不是有意而为之。到目前为止，她甚至不能确定自己对自己的尊重程度，也不能确定其合理性。她认识他才两周。她在梅里顿和他一起跳了四支舞；有一天早上，她在他自己的家里见到了他。家，并且已经与他共进过四次饭，这还不足以让她了解他的性格。”

column1: “Well,” said Charlotte, “I wish Jane success with all my heart; and if she were married to him to-morrow, I should think she had as good a chance of happiness as if she were to be studying his character for a twelvemonth. Happiness in marriage is entirely a matter of chance. If the dispositions of the parties are ever so well known to each other, or ever so similar beforehand, it does not advance their felicity in the least. They always continue to grow sufficiently unlike afterwards to have their share of vexation; and it is better to know as little as possible of the defects of the person with whom you are to pass your life.”
column2: “好吧，”夏洛说，“我衷心祝愿简成功。如果她明天嫁给他，我想她就有很大的机会获得幸福，就好像她要花十二个月的时间研究他的性格一样。婚姻的幸福完全是一个机会问题。如果双方的性格在事前彼此如此了解，或者之前如此相似，那根本不会增加他们的幸福感。他们总是会在事后变得越来越不同，从而拥有自己的那份幸福。”烦恼；最好尽可能少地了解与你共度一生的人的缺点。”

column1: Occupied in observing Mr. Bingley’s attention to her sister, Elizabeth was far from suspecting that she was herself becoming an object of some interest in the eyes of his friend. Mr. Darcy had at first scarcely allowed her to be pretty: he had looked at her without admiration at the ball; and when they next met, he looked at her only to criticise. But no sooner had he made it clear to himself and his friends that she had hardly a good feature in her face, than he began to find it was rendered uncommonly intelligent by the beautiful expression of her dark eyes. To this discovery succeeded some others equally mortifying. Though he had detected with a critical eye more than one failure of perfect symmetry in her form, he was forced to acknowledge her figure to be light and pleasing; and in spite of his asserting that her manners were not those of the fashionable world, he was caught by their easy playfulness. Of this she was perfectly unaware: to her he was only the man who made himself agreeable nowhere, and who had not thought her handsome enough to dance with.
column2: 伊丽莎白专注于观察彬格莱先生对她妹妹的关注，丝毫没有怀疑她自己正在成为他朋友眼中的一个感兴趣的对象。达西先生一开始几乎不承认她漂亮：在舞会上他看着她，脸上并没有钦佩之情。当他们下次见面时，他看着她只是为了批评。但他一向自己和朋友们表明，她的脸上几乎没有什么好看的特征，他就开始发现，她黑眼睛的美丽表情使她的脸变得异常聪明。继这一发现之后，还有其他一些同样令人羞愧的发现。尽管他以挑剔的眼光发现了她身材上不止一处完美对称的缺陷，但他不得不承认她的身材轻盈而令人愉悦；尽管他声称她的举止不符合时尚界的举止，但他还是被她轻松的俏皮所吸引。对于这一点，她完全没有意识到：对她来说，他只是一个让自己在任何地方都讨人喜欢的男人，并且不认为她英俊到可以和她跳舞。

column1: He began to wish to know more of her; and, as a step towards conversing with her himself, attended to her conversation with others. His doing so drew her notice. It was at Sir William Lucas’s, where a large party were assembled.

column1: “You are a very strange creature by way of a friend!--always wanting me to play and sing before anybody and everybody! If my vanity had taken a musical turn, you would have been invaluable; but as it is, I would really rather not sit down before those who must be in the habit of hearing the very best performers.” On Miss Lucas’s persevering, however, she added, “Very well; if it must be so, it must.” And gravely glancing at Mr. Darcy, “There is a very fine old saying, which everybody here is of course familiar with--‘Keep your breath to cool your porridge,’--and I shall keep mine to swell my song.”
column2: “作为朋友，你是一个非常奇怪的生物！——总是希望我在任何人和所有人面前演奏和唱歌！如果我的虚荣心转向音乐，你将是无价的；但事实上，我真的不愿意坐在那些必须习惯于聆听最优秀表演者的人面前。”然而，对于卢卡斯小姐的坚持，她补充道：“很好；如果必须如此，那就必须如此。”并严肃地看了达西先生一眼，“有一句非常优美的老话，这里的每个人当然都熟悉——‘屏住呼吸，让粥冷却’——而我将保留我的呼吸，以增强我的歌声。”
